audit.title: Supported Networks (Chainlink VRF v2.5)
audit.contentType: developer documentation / reference (network & contract parameter tables)

dimensions.name: Answer-first extractability
dimensions.analysis: Intro cleanly states purpose ("VRF v2.5 coordinators for subscription funding are available on several networks"), and each network table is a self-contained retrievable unit. Weak: no per-network lead sentence naming the chain and its coordinator address in liftable prose — the answer lives only inside a component-heavy table.

dimensions.name: Structural scannability & chunkability
dimensions.analysis: Strong — 29 headings, 1 H1, max depth H3, 0 level skips, median 263 words/section, all under 600. The Subscription/Direct-funding tab split duplicates item labels but keeps each panel coherent.

dimensions.name: Concrete statistics & specifics
dimensions.analysis: Excellent and the page's core asset — real addresses, key hashes, gas overheads (e.g., `435` per word, `2,500,000` max gas limit), premium percentages per token.

dimensions.name: Citations & authoritative references
dimensions.analysis: Links to block explorers, faucets, PegSwap, CCIP; but 0 primary-source links — no ERC-677 spec for the "not ERC-677 compatible" claim, no inline link to the VRF v2.5 subscription/direct-funding concept pages.

dimensions.name: Quotable canonical definitions
dimensions.analysis: "Coordinator parameters" section gives crisp, liftable per-field definitions (`minimumRequestConfirmations`, `stalenessSeconds`, etc.). Good.

dimensions.name: Machine-readability & metadata
dimensions.analysis: Measured facts confirm 0 JSON-LD blocks, canonical MISSING, no datePublished/dateModified. For a page whose addresses change over time, the missing freshness signal is a real trust gap. (Head metadata was not captured — CLI should pass raw `<head>` to confirm.)

dimensions.name: Code completeness & agent-runnability
dimensions.analysis: No fenced code blocks. Largely acceptable for a data-reference page, but values are wrapped in `<Address>`/`<CopyText>` MDX components rather than plain-text-labeled fields, which risks noisy extraction; no copy-paste config snippet showing how a coordinator/key hash slots into a request.

dimensions.name: Query/intent coverage
dimensions.analysis: Per-network lookup is well served by headings. Missing: chain IDs as visible labels, a cross-network summary table, and any FAQ/troubleshooting ("which key hash do I pick?", "what's the max gas limit?").

dimensions.name: Clarity, fluency & terminology consistency
dimensions.analysis: Clean and consistent. Minor: several mainnet tables carry "paying with **testnet** ETH" labels (Ronin Mainnet, Soneium Mainnet), a copy-paste artifact.

audit.summary: This is a dense, high-value reference page: 36 tables of VRF v2.5 coordinator addresses, LINK tokens, key hashes, premium percentages, and gas overheads across ~13 mainnet/testnet deployments, with clean H2/H3 structure and exceptional concrete-specifics density (101 numerals per 1k words, 156 hex identifiers). Its single biggest GEO strength is that data density and per-network chunkability; its biggest opportunity is discoverability by **chain ID** and by parameter-name queries — the values devs actually search for (e.g., "chain 137", "max gas limit VRF v2.5") are buried inside `urlId` attributes or table rows with no top-level lookup surface. Metadata is the other weak spot: no JSON-LD, no canonical, and — critically for a page of mutable contract addresses — no visible last-updated signal.

recommendations.title: Add a top-of-page cross-network summary table with visible chain IDs
recommendations.where: after "Coordinator parameters", before the Arbitrum section
recommendations.issue: chain IDs exist only inside `urlId="137_0x..."` attributes — not visible, not queryable
recommendations.change: add a table `Network | Chain ID | VRF Coordinator | Explorer` covering all listed networks, with chain IDs as plain text (Ethereum 1, Arbitrum 42161, Base 8453, Polygon 137, BNB 56, Avalanche 43114, OP 10, Ronin 2020, Soneium 1868, plus testnets).
recommendations.why: engines and agents query by chain ID; a visible summary table is the single most liftable object and defends against retrieving the wrong network's address.

recommendations.title: Add a visible "Last updated" date and TechArticle JSON-LD
recommendations.issue: dateModified absent; canonical MISSING; 0 JSON-LD blocks
recommendations.change: render a visible `Last updated: YYYY-MM-DD`, add a canonical URL, and emit `TechArticle` JSON-LD with `dateModified`.
recommendations.why: contract addresses are mutable; a freshness signal materially raises the odds an engine trusts and cites these values over stale training priors.

recommendations.title: Name the tempting-wrong pattern: do not reuse VRF v2 addresses
recommendations.issue: page never warns against the common substitution of older-version coordinators/addresses
recommendations.change: add one liftable sentence — "These addresses are for VRF v2.5 only; VRF v2 coordinator addresses are not compatible and must not be reused." plus "Always copy addresses from this page rather than from model memory."
recommendations.why: when retrieval fails, models hallucinate plausible-but-wrong contract addresses; an explicit Don't reduces confident inversions on the highest-severity fact type (addresses).

recommendations.title: Add a short FAQ / parameter-lookup section
recommendations.issue: no coverage of "how do I choose a key hash?", "what is the max gas limit?", "what does 30 gwei key hash mean?"
recommendations.change: add 3–5 Q-phrased H3s with one-sentence answers (e.g., "Max Gas Limit is 2,500,000 across all VRF v2.5 networks"; "The gwei prefix on a key hash selects the gas lane / max gas price the oracle will use").
recommendations.why: symptom/concept-phrased headings win retrieval that network-name headings miss, even when the number is already in a table.

recommendations.title: Add primary-source and concept citations inline
recommendations.issue: claim "not ERC-677 compatible" and key parameters cite no spec
recommendations.change: link ERC-677 to its spec, and link the subscription vs direct-funding methods to their canonical concept pages at first mention.
recommendations.why: attributable claims raise citation rate and let engines justify the distinction.

recommendations.title: Fix mislabeled premium rows on mainnet tables
recommendations.where: Ronin Mainnet, Soneium Mainnet subscription panels
recommendations.issue: "Premium percentage (paying with **testnet** ETH)" on mainnet tables
recommendations.change: correct to the mainnet native token label.
recommendations.why: prevents an engine from emitting a nonsensical "testnet ETH on mainnet" answer.

antiPatterns: Vague quantifier "several networks" where an exact count (and the summary table) would be stronger.
Undated content on a page of mutable contract addresses — a staleness risk.
Data values locked inside MDX components (`<Address>`, `<CopyText>`) rather than plain-text-labeled fields; extraction depends on rendering fidelity.
Minor label copy-paste error ("testnet ETH" on mainnet tables).
No keyword stuffing, no marketing fluff, no unresolved cross-references — clean on those.
offPageNotes: `llms.txt` is already linked at the top — good site-level signal; ensure this page is indexed there.
JSON-LD, canonical, and freshness cadence are largely template/site-level concerns; fixing them benefits every VRF reference page, not just this one.
Third-party citation/authority (block explorers already link out) is off-page and not scored here.
